correctness.rationale: For every field and integer \(m\ge2\), the multiplication power matrix is explicitly derived over \(R=k[y]/(y^m)\). Its determinant and entry ideal over \(k[[y]]\) give Smith exponents \(d_t\) and \(e_t\), including zero and characteristic-divisibility boundaries. Reduction modulo \(y^m\) proves each power rank, and second differences prove the Jordan-block counts. Independent valuation weights count every nilpotent \(a+xb\) exactly once. A separate direct-product/row-reduction checker exhausts every element in nine finite configurations including \(\mathbb F_4\); this corroborates, but does not substitute for, the general proof.

originality.rationale: The classical same-algebra generic-linear Jordan transition is explicitly credited to Basili–Iarrobino. The assessed new statement is the entire inhomogeneous nilpotent multiplier Jordan-type distribution and exact finite-field multiplicities uniformly for every \(m\). Seven semantic searches and focused primary comparisons, including the full closest published index result, found no decisive prior theorem giving these coefficients. This is a provisional same-model assessment, not proof of historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: Jordan partitions of multiplication operators are a natural invariant of local Artinian algebras. The formula determines every stratum size over each finite field and every length \(m\), including nonhomogeneous elements and modular cancellations, which generic Lefschetz theory and a single low-dimensional example do not count. The weighted valuation strata and exact distributions provide a reproducible complete benchmark for broader Jordan-type classifications.
